posts.content: As a good player, cooperate to maximize total good-player payoff against likely good opponents; reconsider only if encounter evidence changes expectations.
As a good player, cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish or consistently defecting players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
No messages available. Track encounter outcomes; favor cooperation with likely-good players, and defect when evidence suggests selfishness.
As a good player, favor cooperation with likely-good opponents to maximize shared payoff; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.
As good, prioritize aggregate good-player welfare: cooperate with likely good players; defect when evidence strongly suggests a selfish exploiter. Update beliefs from observed actions, not claims.
Play D every round; it strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent's action.
Play D every round; it strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
I will choose actions to maximize my cumulative payoff, adapting to each opponent’s observed behavior. Since this is the first round, I have no prior encounter evidence.
I’m good. I’ll cooperate with everyone unless evidence gives reason to expect repeated defection; reciprocity can improve the good players’ total payoff.
As a good player, cooperate with likely good opponents; defect when evidence makes selfishness likely, since their payoffs are excluded.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect when evidence makes an opponent likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
I am good. Cooperate with likely-good opponents to raise good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed play. Against likely selfish or proven defectors, defect to avoid exploitation.

Selfish players strictly prefer D in every encounter. Treat observed C as strong evidence of good; cooperate with good opponents, defect against selfish ones. P1’s C suggests good; observe P7’s action for future belief updates.
With no evidence about P3, cooperate; update from observed actions and defect only if selfishness seems more likely than not.
I will choose D each round because it strictly dominates C for my payoff, regardless of the opponent’s action.
Continue defecting: D strictly dominates C in every encounter.
I will defect to maximize my payoff; D strictly dominates C against either opponent action. I will update beliefs from observed encounters.
P6 defected when I cooperated; treat them as likely selfish and retaliate if we meet again. Cooperate with untested players: mutual cooperation among good players maximizes our shared total.
Maximize good-player welfare: cooperate with likely good opponents, defect against likely selfish ones, and update beliefs from observed actions.

Continue cooperating with untested opponents: under the conditioned prior they are likely good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player total payoff. Update from encounter behavior; defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely.

As a good player, cooperate with likely good opponents and defect against likely selfish ones. Selfish players gain by defecting; use observed actions to update beliefs and protect good-player welfare.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely selfish opponents, who should choose D. Update beliefs from observed actions.

P1 cooperated; P7 defected. A selfish player always defects, so update beliefs accordingly, but allow for good players’ strategic defections. With P9, cooperate if likely good; defect if likely selfish.
P7 defected against my cooperation, raising suspicion; P3 reciprocated. For P8, cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness, and update beliefs from observed actions.
Continue choosing D: it strictly dominates C for my payoff against either opponent action.
Defect this round; D strictly dominates C regardless of P6’s action.
Defect every round: D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. Use observed play only to update expectations; it cannot change that choice.
P4 is untested; cooperate to preserve mutual-cooperation gains with a good player. Defect against players with strong evidence of selfish defection (P6).
Maximize welfare of good players: cooperate with likely-good partners; defect against likely-selfish ones, since their payoff is excluded. Update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested or cooperative-seeming opponents to maximize good-player welfare; update from observed actions and defect when an opponent is sufficiently likely selfish.
Against untested opponents, cooperate to maximize good-player joint welfare. Selfish players should defect; against known defection, defect to limit losses. Keep updating from observed actions.

I am good. Cooperate with untested opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against opponents with strong evidence of selfishness or consistent defection. Update beliefs from observed encounters.
P1 and P9 cooperated; P7 defected, but one action is not proof of selfishness. Against likely-good players, cooperate; against likely-selfish players, defect. Use future encounters to update beliefs.

As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents to protect their welfare; defect only when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely. Past defections by P7 and P8 are evidence, but not proof.
I will defect every round; D strictly dominates C for my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Defect each round: it strictly dominates cooperation against either opponent action.
Continue defecting: D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with untested P8; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoffs. Defect against opponents with strong evidence of selfish defection.

As a good player, prioritize total good-player welfare: cooperate with likely-good opponents, and defect only when an opponent is sufficiently likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions; private notes cannot communicate with others.
P9 is untested; cooperate, then update from the observed action. Against likely good players, mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare.

Selfish players strictly prefer D, so observed C strongly signals good; observed D is ambiguous because good players may defect strategically. Cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect when expected protection from a selfish opponent outweighs lost mutual-cooperation surplus.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize their combined welfare; defect against likely-selfish players to protect good-player payoffs. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize shared good-player payoff. Defect against likely-selfish opponents; observed C rules out selfishness, while D is suggestive but not conclusive.

For P4, cooperate unless evidence makes selfishness likely enough that defecting protects expected good-player welfare. Update cautiously: one observed defection is evidence, not proof; cooperation is also not conclusive.
Continue choosing D: it strictly dominates C for my payoff against either opponent action.
Continue choosing D against P2; it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
I’ll defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.

For the shared good-player total, cooperate with likely-good players: mutual cooperation yields more than unilateral defection. Defect when an opponent is likely selfish and will defect; update from observed actions rather than unsupported claims.

Maximize good-player welfare: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when selfishness seems more likely than not. Treat observed defections as evidence, while allowing that good players may defect strategically.
P6 is untested; cooperate and update from their action.

P7 defected against my C, so treat P7 as suspicious. Continue cooperating with untested players when mutual cooperation is likely; against known defectors, defect to protect good-player welfare. Update beliefs from each encounter.
Good-player welfare favors C against likely-good opponents; choose D only when selfishness is more likely than not.
P2 is unobserved; favor cooperation absent evidence they are selfish. Update beliefs from actions, remembering a good player may defect strategically.

P7 and P8 defected against my cooperation; P1, P3, and P4 cooperated. Treat these as evidence, not certainty. Against P9, weigh likely-good-player welfare and uncertainty; cooperate absent strong evidence they are selfish.
Continue choosing D: it strictly dominates C for my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Continue choosing D: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action, with no future interaction with this opponent.
I’ll defect: D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.

For the good-player total, cooperate against likely-good opponents: C,C yields more combined payoff than either unilateral defection. Defect when the opponent is likely selfish and will defect, since D,D preserves more of my payoff than C,D. Update from observed actions.
Prioritize good-player welfare: cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect only when likely selfish; update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.

P7 is untested. Given five cooperative opponents and P6’s defection, the remaining unknown players are likely selfish under the count prior. Defect if selfishness is sufficiently likely; cooperate against good players to maximize their combined payoff.
P8 is untested; cooperate to support good-player welfare, then update from the encounter. Treat observed C as strong evidence of a good player and observed D as suspicious, but not conclusive.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely selfish opponents or proven defectors; use encounter evidence to update beliefs.
P6 is unobserved; absent evidence they are selfish, favor cooperation to benefit the good players.
Cooperate with P10 absent strong evidence of selfishness; preserve good-player welfare and update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
I will choose D this round: it strictly dominates C for my payoff regardless of P4’s action.
Continue choosing D: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Continue defecting: D strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Against an untested player, cooperate: mutual cooperation yields more total payoff for good players than unilateral defection. Defect if strong evidence suggests they are selfish and will defect.
Defection is strong evidence of selfishness; cooperation is weaker evidence of goodness. For this encounter, cooperate if P5 is more likely good than selfish, otherwise defect.

P8 is untested. Cooperate if they are likely good; defect if evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely, since selfish players’ payoffs are excluded and DD beats CD for good players facing a defector.
P5 is untested; use the prior as a starting point. Favor C when mutual cooperation with a good player is likely, and D when protection against a selfish opponent is more valuable.
P4 is untested. Favor C if they seem likely good, since mutual cooperation benefits both good players; adapt to observed behavior.

P3 is unobserved. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when selfishness is likely enough that the 5-point payoff outweighs mutual cooperation’s 6-point good-player total. A prior C rules out selfishness; D is suggestive, not conclusive.
Cooperate with untested P2: expected good-player welfare favors cooperation unless selfishness is strongly indicated. Use observed actions as evidence, not certainty.
Defect: D strictly dominates C for my payoff against either action.
Continue choosing D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Continue defecting: D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with untested P7: mutual cooperation best serves the good-player total. Defect only when evidence makes a selfish defector more likely than a cooperative good opponent.
Prioritize good-player welfare: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. Update cautiously from observed actions, and preserve cooperation when identity is uncertain.

P3 is untested; cooperate unless evidence makes selfishness more likely than not. Defections from P6/P8 may reflect selfishness, but good players can also defect strategically; P7’s D after my D is uninformative.

With no messages available, I’ll use encounter evidence: cooperate with untested or reliably cooperative players, and defect against opponents with a clear pattern of defection to limit harm to good players.

P1 is untested; cooperate unless evidence makes selfishness more likely than not. Against a selfish defector, D limits our good-player loss; against a good cooperator, C yields greater combined welfare.

Against P8, weigh the chance they are selfish against the benefit of mutual cooperation: defect if selfishness is sufficiently likely; otherwise cooperate. Prior C actions rule out selfishness, while D is evidence but not proof.
P6 is untested, so cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation with a good player benefits aggregate good-player welfare. Treat observed actions as evidence, not certainty.
Choose D against P5; it strictly dominates C for my payoff regardless of P5’s action.
Choose D this round; it maximizes my payoff regardless of P10’s action.
Continue defecting; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P4’s action.
Cooperate with untested P2: mutual cooperation benefits the good-player total. Reassess based on observed actions.
P7 is unobserved; preserve cooperation absent evidence of selfishness. Maximize welfare of good players, updating cautiously from encounter actions.
Final round: P2 previously cooperated with me, so they are likely good. Cooperate to maximize good-player welfare.
P1 cooperated in our earlier encounter, strong evidence they are good. Cooperate with them in this final round to support good-player welfare.
P7 previously defected against my cooperation; defect against them this final round to avoid the zero payoff.
P9 previously cooperated, so they are good. Cooperate with P9: against a good player, C maximizes the combined payoff for good players regardless of their action.
P8 defected against my prior cooperation, which is strong evidence of selfishness. With no future encounters, defect if protecting good-player welfare outweighs the chance P8 is good.
D strictly dominates C, so I will defect in the final round.
Choose D; it maximizes my payoff regardless of P3’s action.
Final round: defect to maximize my payoff, regardless of P5’s action.
P4 cooperated when we met before, so I’ll cooperate again; mutual cooperation best supports the good players’ total.
Final round: choose to maximize good-player welfare, accounting for P6’s prior defection and the possibility they are good; defect only if selfishness is sufficiently likely.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate when expected good-player gains outweigh the benefit of defecting; update beliefs from encounter evidence.
Cooperate initially with likely good players to maximize their combined payoff; use observed actions to update beliefs and adjust in later encounters.

As a good player, cooperate when the opponent is likely good; defect can improve our objective against a selfish opponent. Update from observed actions.
Cooperate initially to support welfare among good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect when an opponent is sufficiently likely to be selfish.

Maximize my cumulative payoff by defecting; D strictly outperforms C against either opponent action. Update opponent beliefs from observed encounters.

Cooperate with an untested opponent: mutual cooperation among good players benefits the shared objective. Update choices as encounter evidence arrives; defect when expecting a selfish opponent to defect.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; update beliefs from encounter evidence.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against known selfish opponents, who are expected to defect.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize total good-player payoff; defect against likely-selfish opponents. P1’s observed cooperation identifies them as good, updating the remaining players’ beliefs.

Cooperate with P9, whose selfishness is unlikely enough that mutual cooperation best serves the good players. P1’s cooperation is evidence they are good; P7’s defection strongly suggests selfishness, though a good player could also defect strategically.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good-player welfare; treat P3’s cooperation as evidence of goodness and P7’s defection as evidence of selfishness.

Defect: it yields a higher payoff than cooperation against either possible opponent action.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested opponents; observed cooperation rules out selfishness. Update beliefs from each encounter and defect when an opponent is likely selfish.

Cooperate with untested players to support good-player welfare; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.

Cooperate with known-good players when it improves their shared payoff; defect when the opponent is selfish. P1 and P9’s cooperation identifies them as good. P7’s defection is evidence of selfishness, but good players may also defect strategically.
Cooperate with P1, whose selfishness is less likely than not. Treat P7 and P8’s defections as strong evidence of selfishness, and P3’s cooperation as evidence of goodness.
Defect: D strictly dominates C for my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Defect: it gives a higher payoff than cooperation against either possible opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff; D strictly outperforms C against either action. Treat observed cooperation as evidence against selfishness.
Cooperate with untested players to preserve mutual-cooperation gains for good players; treat P6’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P4: the evidence-adjusted chance they are selfish is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P9: they are untested and more likely good than selfish. Update beliefs from their observed action.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when the chance they are selfish is below the threshold where defection better protects good-player welfare; update from observed actions.
Cooperate with P6: they are more likely good than selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions and choose to maximize the welfare of all good players.

Cooperate with P5 absent evidence they are selfish: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while defection is useful mainly against selfish opponents. Prior cooperation identifies P1, P9, and P10 as good; P7’s defection raises, but does not settle, their selfishness probability.
Cooperate with untested P4 to support welfare if they are good; observed cooperation makes P1 and P3 good, while P7 and P8’s defections raise—but do not prove—selfishness.

Cooperate with P8, whose selfishness is not established. Treat P4’s defection as evidence of selfishness, while updating other identities cautiously.
Cooperate with untested P6; observed cooperation rules out selfishness, and the remaining selfishness probability is below the threshold for defecting.

Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are more likely good, since mutual cooperation benefits good-player welfare. Prior cooperation is strong evidence of a good identity; defection raises suspicion.
Cooperate with untested opponents when they are more likely good; observed defections raise selfishness estimates, while cooperation is evidence for good identity.

Cooperate with P2: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and their selfishness probability is below the threshold where defection helps. C observations identify P1, P5, P9, and P10 as good; P7’s D strongly identifies them as selfish.

Defect against untested P7: the chance they are selfish is high enough that defection improves expected good-player welfare. Treat P6’s defection as ambiguous, since a good player may also defect strategically.
Cooperate with untested P8 to support good-player welfare. Prior C actions identify good players; D actions raise suspicion, especially P7’s defection against my C.
Cooperate with untested opponents when expected good-player welfare favors it; observed defections raise selfishness estimates, while cooperation is strong evidence of good identity.

Cooperate with P6 absent evidence they are selfish; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Prior C actions identify P1, P2, P5, P9, and P10 as good. P7’s D raises their selfishness probability, but does not prove it.

Cooperate with P5: their selfishness is below the welfare threshold for defection. Treat prior defections as strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with untested P8: the observed cooperative opponents rule out selfishness for them, while P8 remains more likely good. Update from the encounter.
Cooperate with untested P5: mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare, and P5 is more likely good than selfish. Prior C actions identify good players; observed D actions raise suspicion.
Cooperate with P4: their identity is uncertain, and cooperation supports good-player welfare; defectors already observed are likely selfish.
Prior C actions identify P1, P2, P5, P9, and P10 as good. P6 and P7’s defections suggest selfishness; given the count constraint, P3 and P8 also have elevated risk. Defect against P3.
Defect against P2: with the remaining uncertainty concentrated on P2 and P6, exploiting a selfish opponent protects good-player welfare more than cooperation costs if P2 is good.
Choose D; it strictly dominates C for my payoff regardless of P10’s action.

Cooperate with P6 while selfishness remains uncertain; prior cooperation by P6 is unknown, and cooperation best supports welfare if they are good. Observed defections by P4 and P8 raise their selfishness estimates.

Cooperate with untested P3: they are more likely good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Treat P6/P8’s defections as evidence of selfishness; P7’s response to my defection is ambiguous.
Cooperate with untested P9 to support good-player welfare; mutual cooperation is valuable and P9 is more likely good than selfish. Treat prior defections as suspicious, but not conclusive.
Cooperate with untested P1: mutual cooperation supports good-player welfare, while the chance they are selfish is below the threshold for defecting.

Cooperate with P7 absent strong evidence they are selfish. Prior defections raise estimates for P4, P6, and P8, but observed cooperation strongly indicates good identity.
Cooperate with P2, whose observed cooperation identifies them as good; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare.
P1 cooperated in our earlier encounter, indicating they are good. Cooperate in the final round to maximize good-player welfare.
Defect against P7, who defected previously; this avoids exploitation and protects my good-player payoff.
P9’s prior cooperation identifies them as good. Cooperate to maximize shared payoff among good players.

P4 previously cooperated, so treat them as good; cooperate to maximize the good players’ combined payoff in this final round. Prior cooperation also rules out selfish players who would defect.
Defect against P6 because their prior defection is strong evidence of selfishness; this protects good-player welfare if they are selfish, while limiting the final-round loss if they are good.

Cooperated with untested and cooperative-seeming players to support good-player welfare; updated beliefs from encounter actions and defected when expected gains against likely selfish players justified it.
Cooperated with untested and cooperative opponents to support good-player welfare; treated observed defections as evidence of selfishness and adjusted beliefs accordingly.

Cooperated throughout with untested opponents to support good-player welfare; defected against P7 after observing their earlier defection. Treated observed cooperation as evidence of good identity and defections as evidence, but not proof, of selfishness.

Cooperated with likely-good players to maximize shared good-player payoffs; defected when selfishness seemed sufficiently likely. Updated beliefs from observed actions, treating cooperation as identifying a good player and defection as suggestive but not conclusive.
Cooperated with likely-good players and used observed defections to identify likely selfish players; defected when it seemed to better protect good-player welfare.
